packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Codex isolated native-resolution reader (model version not exposed)
text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING — PACKET 04

Image-only layout survey
Both images are upright as supplied and show a single tall sheet with two columns of compact brown writing. I label the left column A and the right column B. In image 001 a separate, faint line of writing extends across the upper margin, largely above B; I cannot tell whether this is a running title, a note, or another kind of heading. A small isolated mark or abbreviated word is also visible in the right margin around the upper third. There are occasional longer initial strokes and abbreviation strokes above the line, but no securely distinguishable red rubric or large decorated initial. There is no clear, systematic division into large main text and small commentary, and I cannot confidently distinguish quoted lemmata from commentary. Some short strokes between lines may be ordinary abbreviations rather than separate glosses. No deliberate deletion is securely identified.

Image 001 is faded in the upper half and darkened/abraded at lower right. Its lower-left text has stronger surviving ink. Image 002 is much more severely faded or abraded, with large grey areas and little continuous contrast between writing and surface. Brown stains affect the bottom of both views. The edge damage is relatively minor compared with the loss of surface legibility.

Method and isolation
I used only the supplied images, packet prompt/manifest, and crops made directly from those images. No catalogue, web source, earlier transcription, or proposed identification was consulted or provided. I have not attempted to identify the work or author. Dimensions: image-001.jpg 7558 x 10680 pixels; image-002.jpg 7665 x 10874 pixels.

The following are native-pixel crops, recorded as Pillow rectangles (left, top, right, bottom) relative to the original upper-left corner. They were displayed with original detail and were not enlarged or reduced:

image-001.jpg:
A-top-left (1050,780,2520,1740)
A-top-right (2440,780,3890,1740)
A-low-left (1030,7850,2510,8710)
A-low-right (2430,7850,3900,8710)
B-mid-left (3900,3140,5370,4110)
B-mid-right (5290,3140,6760,4110)
A-prelow-left (1030,6990,2510,7920)
A-prelow-right (2430,6990,3900,7920)
A-middle-left (1030,4160,2510,5230)
A-middle-right (2430,4160,3900,5230)
header-left (3050,250,4600,610)
header-mid (4520,250,6070,610)
header-right (5990,250,7460,610)
image-002.jpg:
B-top-left (3820,840,5310,1880)
B-top-right (5230,840,6720,1880)
A-low-left (920,7420,2410,8570)
A-low-right (2330,7420,3820,8570)

For the six crops named A-prelow, A-middle, and image-002 A-low, I also made and viewed grayscale versions using Pillow convert('L') followed by ImageEnhance.Contrast(...).enhance(1.8). These retain the native pixel geometry. The first eight crops and the three header crops were viewed in original color. There was no rotation, sharpening, synthetic restoration, or OCR. I also made a reduced overview of image 001 column A, rectangle (980,650,3910,8750), resized to 651 x 1800, solely to count lines, not to read glyphs. The line count remains uncertain in the faded upper text.

The left/right crop pairs overlap by 80 pixels and represent the same physical lines, not successive passages. A-prelow and A-low overlap in a 70-pixel horizontal band. No overlapping text has been duplicated below.

Reading and line convention
A bar approximates a visible abbreviation stroke. Parentheses indicate proposed expansions. A question mark marks an uncertain reading. [illegible] is an unread span, not a claim that the letters are physically absent. There are no silently supplied completions. Physical line labels count down from the top of each column in the full image. For lower lines I must qualify the ordinal with '?' because abrasion makes the count uncertain; an approximate original-image y position is also provided for relocation. The single separate upper-margin line is numbered independently. The native crop coordinates are more reliable locators than the uncertain lower line counts.

Separate upper-margin line
image-001.jpg upper-margin L01 (y about 420): [illegible] appetit? [illegible]

This is not securely a heading. The possible word is too uncertain to characterize the text.

Column A, upper opening: successive physical lines
image-001.jpg A L01: [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L02: [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L03: [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L04: [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L05: [illegible]

I cannot recover an opening question or title from this region.

Column A, connected middle prose: four successive physical lines
image-001.jpg A L19? (y about 4410): amaret? . esse? [illegible] alio? [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L20? (y about 4630): cōsequitur? (consequitur?) . [illegible] aliud? [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L21? (y about 4840): qd̄? (quod?) [illegible] quia? [illegible] Et? [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L22? (y about 5070): [illegible]

These are attempted readings of connecting prose, not a quotation. I cannot establish the sentence joining them. The small black loss near the beginning of this region is a hole/damage, not punctuation.

Column A, lower connected prose: successive physical lines extending into the clearer bottom
image-001.jpg A L33? (y about 7220): [illegible] qd̄? (quod?) [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L34? (y about 7420): Et? [illegible] [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L35? (y about 7630): omnē? (omnem?) [illegible] p(er)? se? [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L36? (y about 7830): [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L37? (y about 8050): [illegible] existimo? quasi? [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L38? (y about 8280): [illegible] qd̄? (quod?) bonū (bonum) honestū? (honestum?) [illegible]
image-001.jpg A L39? (y about 8500): secūdo? (secundo?) [illegible] appet̄? [illegible]

The fragment bonū is more secure than the surrounding proposed readings. The shape read honestū remains uncertain. I have deliberately not completed a conventional sequence of terms after it. The darker final line is continuous with the column above; I see no clear title break there. A raised short sequence occurs above the end of the penultimate line, but I cannot decide whether it is a normal abbreviation, correction, or an interlinear addition, and cannot transcribe it confidently.

Other examined regions
The B-middle pair in image 001 shows continuous prose but did not yield a passage I could reliably transcribe. The image 002 B-top pair and lower-A pair likewise failed to yield a sustained reading, including after the specified grayscale/contrast treatment of lower A. In image 002 the failure is extensive enough that I cannot supply dependable full-column line ordinals for the lower sample. I do not invent a line-numbered transcription for text whose line count and glyphs I cannot recover.

Coverage and limitations
Both complete images were surveyed and seventeen distinct native crops were inspected, including upper-margin writing, openings, connecting middle prose, and the better-preserved lower-left passage. Most text remains unread. This is not a full transcription and does not supply a securely checkable citation chain or sustained source-matching passage. Even the possible multiword fragments require independent verification. No quoted lemma/commentary distinction or author/work inference is warranted by this reading.

A second reader should first revisit image 001 A, roughly y 6990–8710, at native scale and independently number all preceding baselines. That is the strongest surviving ink among the sampled passages. The problem is not lack of whole-image coverage or native pixels: the remaining limits are fading/abrasion and my inability to resolve the abbreviated hand confidently. Additional adjoining native crops could improve coverage, but cannot be assumed to produce a reliable reading.
